themes.title: Capital markets start pricing the AI infra risk premium
themes.summary: The first cracks in the AI build-out trade are showing up in credit and equity markets: derivatives volumes hedging big-tech debt are surging, insurers are funding data-center loans, and a South Korean neocloud IPO flopped before bouncing. Ken Griffin calls the AI run 'almost certainly' a bubble. For CFOs the signal is clear: the cost of capital for AI infrastructure is starting to discriminate, and capex plans need re-underwriting.
themes.angle: The AI trade is being repriced from growth to credit risk; watch CDS spreads.

themes.title: Gulf sovereign AI: from check-writing to board control
themes.summary: The Gulf is moving beyond buying compute and stakes: G42 signed nonbinding pacts with Yann LeCun's AMI Labs for physical and industrial AI, and regional wealth funds are reportedly seeking tighter control over their AI bets. ADGM is pulling in global financial firms, and Saudi regulators launched a deepfake-awareness push. The region is shifting from investor to operator and governor of AI.
themes.angle: Gulf AI strategy is maturing from deal count to board control.

themes.title: OpenAI goes vertical: agents for biotech and finance
themes.summary: OpenAI acquired Orchestra Bio, a startup whose agents help pharma manage drug development, and separately showed GPT-6.1 matching senior investor judgment 88.6% of the time on mandate audits at Terminal X. The through-line: frontier labs are selling outcomes in regulated verticals, not just tokens. Life sciences and financial services are the first beachheads.

themes.title: Anthropic's 5.5 wave: cheaper agents, an IPO window
themes.summary: Anthropic shipped Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5, with Opus leading agentic coding and knowledge work at 40% lower cost than Opus 5. It also opened a Singapore office and committed shares to a public-benefit fund. The FT notes the company's listing window is shrinking, making this an unusually full-frontal quarter.

themes.title: Autonomy gets measurable: DeepMind agents clear Minecraft
themes.summary: Google DeepMind's four Gemini 4 Argon agents beat Minecraft's Ender Dragon in 27 hours with no human help, writing 2,783 programs of their own and burning an estimated $520 in tokens through 605 deaths. Picked up by multiple outlets, it is a concrete, cheap benchmark of agentic autonomy. The implied message: long-horizon agency is becoming testable at commodity token prices.
themes.angle: Autonomy benchmarks are becoming measurable - and cheap.

themes.title: The grid is the new GPU: power bottlenecks bite
themes.summary: Goldman Sachs warns energy bottlenecks will stall the AI race; Australian operator NextDC cut guidance by a third after community opposition delayed power; UK banks were hit by a Google Cloud outage; and Musk says ASML is expediting gear for Tesla-SpaceX's Terafab. Compute's binding constraint has moved firmly from silicon to electrons, permits and resilience.

themes.title: Safety, spies and refusals: the AI trust deficit widens
